activity.notes: Kiyomori became Daijō-daijin in 1167 and resigned only about three months later. ATLAS records that formal office as a one-year-granularity Activity instead of converting his broader Taira political dominance into an invented formal reign.

sources.title: Taira no Kiyomori — Japanese Wiki Corpus
sources.citation_text: Japanese Wiki Corpus records Kiyomori's appointment as Daijō-daijin in March 1167 and his resignation roughly three months later.

review_context.namuwiki_review: Related NamuWiki material confirms the historical name in context, but no independently verified exact Person target URL was established; no guessed link.
review_context.chronology_decision: Represent the documented formal Daijō-daijin term at year granularity in 1167; do not broaden it into a de facto reign.
